newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Data lull leads to slide in Bund vol.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Data lull leads to slide in Bund vol.

text.p: Implied volatility headed down in most major contracts in London traded on Monday, taking advantage of a lull in activity in the underlying futures, traders said.
After the cacophony of data last week, including the key U.S. non-farm payrolls, the lack of major releases allowed volatility to slide.
"It's a do nothing day," said Luke White, a broker at FIMAT Futures UK in London. "The major story is that volatility is coming off -- in Bunds, notionnel, BTPs, gilts, Euromarks and short sterling."
He said June Bund option volatility was at 5.83 percent, down from around 5.95 percent at the start of trade on Monday.
A trader at a British brokerage on the LIFFE floor said trade had been limited, leading to a slide in volatility.
She said mid-vol in the April Bund options on the June futures contract was trading at 5.45 percent, after drifting down from 5.85 percent at the open.
"We haven't seen anything major to drive the volatility," she said.

Activity in the Bund options was clustered in the April series. More than 3,200 calls were traded at the 102.00 strike, and almost 1,000 at 102.50. Puts saw predominant activity at strikes from 101.00 to 101.50.
June Bund futures were up 28 basis points at 101.78 by 1530 GMT.
White said sliding volatility was a hang-over from last Friday's U.S. labour market report which was broadly neutral.
Non-farm payrolls rose a stronger than expected 339,000 but average hourly earnings inched up only three cents to $12.09.

White said with scant data releases scheduled for this week, trade on LIFFE was expected to be thin. However, traders said there was still buying interest for volatility, which should put a floor under the market.
